title: Spatial Design Stimuli to Promote Wellness through Buildings' Design
authors: Ramadan, Amal and Kamel Ahmed, Ehab (2019)
review_question: To define a set of all possible architectural design parameters that may affect users' psychological wellbeing within the space.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Literature on healing and supportive environments, psychologically-supportive-design, restorative environment, and user-centred design. Combinations of keywords like 'healing environments AND staff outcomes', 'design AND stress', 'evidence-based design' AND outcomes, 'evidence-based design' AND the physical environment. Disciplines included Psychology, Medicine, and Architecture. Documents dated from 1990 to November 2018, written in English Language.

search_databases: University of Nottingham, Ningbo China [UNNC] library catalogues
University of Nottingham UK [UoN] library catalogues

synthesis_conclusions: Spatial attributes (Spatial Layout, Ergonomics, Privacy, Furniture, Safety & Infection Control, Nature, Views, Light, Colours, Art, Finishing Materials & Textures, Noise & Sounds, Shape & Patterns, Fresh Air & Odours, Water) have an influential impact on human psychology within the spatial environment.
These stimuli, if well employed, create 'positive distraction' for the mind and enhance users' wellbeing, altering a person's frame of mind and creating a positive psychological experience.
The intensity and characteristics of these spatial stimuli should vary depending on the function and nature of the building's users.
Individuals generally prefer medium levels of arousal from stimuli; extreme levels lead to negative emotional impact (Berlyne's optimal arousal theory).
evidence_gaps: Evidence on emotional effects of multisensory stimulation and how interventions elicit desired responses is still scarce and disorganised.
Considerable variations in experimental conditions, methodologies, and measures make it hard to relate findings across studies.
Insufficient evidence to validate a comprehensive framework for multisensory assumptions on effective interventions.
heterogeneity_sources: Experimental conditions, methodologies, and measures used across studies.
limitations: Methodological weakness of studying complex and subjective phenomena (e.g., colour) in isolation.
The ability to formulate multisensory assumptions on effective interventions is yet only hypothetic due to insufficient evidence.
